+# Photo to 3D round 5: measured repair run
+
+Codex (GPT-6) carried out the repair research and verification for
+[task 93](../codex/93-photo-3d-r5.md) on `codex/photo-3d-r5`. The frozen main is
+`5a55f5ccc25ebfa155e5db2391236558feb551ec`, and the protected checkpoint is
+`58f3d8ede13714bf4b3d1f99fbf3b29d7f60e492`.
+
+The Goal began on October 15, 2026, at 9:33 p.m. Eastern (October 16 at 01:33 UTC). The hard stop is
+October 16 at 9:33 a.m. Eastern (13:33 UTC). **The Goal is unmet; no production change qualified.**
+
+## Status of the retained change
+
+| Requirement                                                          | Measured result                                                                                                                                                               |
+| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| Three chosen classes improve by at least 25%                         | Unmet: boundary color error, flat-depth warnings, and ribbons each improve by exactly 0%.                                                                                     |
+| Every other atlas input and checkpoint clip stays the same or better | Preserved: all 118 inputs at both profiles have identical native pixels and quality values; all 49 checkpoint pairs match across the review frames.                           |
+| Phone time and memory do not increase                                | No runtime change is retained. Every tested optimization was cut; the complete phone-cost gate and physical-phone performance are unmeasured.                                 |
+| Sharp works for every input at both profiles                         | Verified for all 118 atlas inputs and 13 additional legacy review inputs, or 131 distinct inputs.                                                                             |
+| Every existing spec passes                                           | All 2,853 runnable tests passed after one failed-job rerun on the cited revision. One existing private-fixture test remains skipped, so every-spec coverage is unestablished. |
+| Ten most-improved and five least-improved review slots               | All 15 slots have recordings. The complete 118-input ranking contains measured zero-improvement ties; no ten actual improvements are claimed.                                 |
+
+The application, sample assets, vendor files, original finder, and existing tests remain unchanged
+from synchronized main. Eight new spec files contain the 26 measurement-method tests. Rejected
+prototype code is archived as text on the unmerged review branch and is not included in the app.
+Final additional repeat coverage is recorded in the linked evidence package and the PR handback;
+partial captures never grant tolerance to an unmeasured case.
+
+## Target selection and correction
+
+The [118-input atlas](photo-3d-failures-2026-10.md) supplies the frozen source hashes, nine poses,
+two profiles, probes, metric definitions, and review levels. A row is one input at one profile. For
+each class, cost is the flagged row count times its mean severity, where severity is the row's worst
+supported pose score divided by that class's existing review level. Equivalently, cost is the sum of
+these ratios over flagged rows. This is a repair-priority heuristic, not a perceptually calibrated
+comparison between unlike units. The initial ranking omitted the atlas's separate flat-depth warning
+filter. Including that filter corrects the three highest costs as follows. This correction does not
+move the original deadline; no production reconstruction change was retained under the initial
+selection.
+
+| Class                                | Flagged / supported rows |        Mean flagged score |     Cost | Intended repair                                                                                                                        |
+| ------------------------------------ | -----------------------: | ------------------------: | -------: | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| Color error at depth boundaries      |                227 / 227 |        13.4661% RGB error | 764.2023 | Inspect source-color ownership and depth-edge registration; preserve text, thin structures, and probe support.                         |
+| Flat-depth T-junction warnings       |                209 / 212 | 56.0372% warned junctions | 585.5884 | Investigate source-supported depth separation with frozen baseline probes; texture junctions alone cannot justify new geometric steps. |
+| Directional ribbons in revealed fill |                211 / 223 | 40.3048 percentage points | 566.9536 | Continue eligible background texture into disocclusions while preserving gradients and believable content.                             |
+
+The remaining costs are texture-energy loss 232.1019, fringe width 195.4848, lost thin-line contrast
+173.5949, memory 138.8500, depth-order warnings 124.1080, cold latency 53.3361, and zero flagged
+holes or default-threshold reference-depth errors. The exploratory 5% reference-depth cutoff has a
+cost of 20.1228 and does not affect the selected targets. Flat-depth and order warnings are
+image-cue hypotheses, not measurements of physical scene depth. Reference errors remain separate.
+Unsupported scores remain unknown. Both profiles and every input remain regression gates.
+
+The atlas examples include the dog's muzzle and ears, the dragonfly, and the long library for
+boundary error; submerged stones, the frozen waterfall, and the fishing cove for flat-depth
+warnings; and the forest path, the still-life painting, and the tabby for ribbons. The exact flagged
+membership and scores are recorded in [the target manifest](photo-3d-r5/targets.json).
+
+## Verification plan
+
+Re-measure frozen main with the original finder, measure repeat noise, and compare candidates using
+the same input hashes and native rendered evidence. Reject any supported per-input regression, lost
+probe support, blank capture, changed test threshold, or phone cost increase. Keep metric
+calibration separate from visual review. Phone-profile software rendering is not a measurement on a
+physical phone. The final handback will distinguish completed checks from missing evidence.
+
+## Measured research
+
+The production reconstruction source is still unchanged. None of the three 25% targets has passed.
+Source-only experiments stay outside the shipping tree until their quality, cost, and motion gates
+pass.
+
+Main advanced to `cc297c89ef4fa4bf04e43196ca3b37e39c97a372` during the run. It was merged into this
+branch without conflicts. That merge changes application lifecycle and unrelated toys, but not the
+Photo to 3D core, relief, depth model, or finder calibration. The original frozen-main study
+completed without changing its measurement source. A fresh full current-source study uses the
+synchronized application rather than mixing captures from different application revisions. All
+production reconstruction source, sample assets, and vendor files remain identical to synchronized
+main; no runtime optimization is retained.
+
+The compressed-index candidate matched every pure-builder output across all 236 input/profile
+combinations, but its isolated forest cost study failed. Five fresh browser observations per build
+produced median/worst first-view times of 4,186/4,631 ms on main and 4,691/9,828 ms on the
+candidate. PSS improved, but the observed time increase fails the gate. It was cut; the
+[observations and hashes](photo-3d-r5/index-cost-rejection.json) remain available. These are
+one-input counterexamples, not a complete-corpus cost measurement or proof of a causal slowdown.
+
+A second exact-output candidate deferred the plain bilinear fallback until the weighted depth gather
+actually needs it. Its [complete comparison](photo-3d-r5/lazy-bilinear-equivalence.json) matched
+every returned property across all 236 builds, plus 32 explicit fallback fixtures. Its
+[isolated cost study](photo-3d-r5/lazy-bilinear-cost-rejection.json) improved median/worst time from
+3,681/4,257 to 2,984/3,938 ms, but increased median/worst PSS from 801/814 to 818/841 MiB, so it was
+cut. Combining it with
+[parent termination of uncached workers](photo-3d-r5/parent-termination-cost-rejection.json) reduced
+memory but increased both time statistics. A separate
+[self-closing worker variant](photo-3d-r5/self-closing-cost-rejection.json) also reduced memory, but
+its observed worst time increased from 3,537 to 3,620 ms. Both were cut. Browser protocol probes
+verified identical returned payloads and surviving transferred bitmap pixels, cached-worker reuse,
+and stale-token fallback; those probes do not replace full-corpus cost and motion checks.
+
+Two later exact-output candidates also failed isolated cost screens. The existing
+[canvas fallback](photo-3d-r5/canvas-fallback-cost-rejection.json) matched all 18 forest native
+poses at both profiles, but median/worst first-view time rose from 2,016/2,267 to 2,344/2,548 ms,
+and worst PSS rose from 841 to 864 MiB. The
+[scratch-gradient cache](photo-3d-r5/scratch-gradient-equivalence.json) matched every prepared and
+unprepared builder output and source-preparation object across all 236 input/profile combinations.
+Its [1,296 direct refiner fixtures](photo-3d-r5/scratch-gradient-fixtures.json) exercised cache
+hits, precision fallback, and boundary fallback, independently matching the pinned original helper
+byte for byte. The separate 32 fixtures in the builder record exercise the unchanged upsampler
+fallback. Its 18-pose native scout was also pixel-exact. Nevertheless, its
+[forest cost screen](photo-3d-r5/scratch-gradient-cost-rejection.json) increased median/worst time
+from 1,628/1,640 to 1,734/1,860 ms and median/worst PSS from 813/852 to 838/852 MiB; the exact worst
+PSS increase was 267,264 bytes. Each screen used five fresh browsers per build with competing local
+audits closed. Both candidates were cut without benchmark retries. These are bounded observed
+rejections, not a full-corpus performance result or a causal slowdown claim.
+[Exact candidate and method bytes, raw cost manifests, and every observation](https://github.com/ryanjosephkamp/splashery/tree/codex/photo-3d-r5-clips/review/photo-3d-r5/rejected-code-research)
+are preserved on the unmerged review branch.
+
+An [identical-source control](photo-3d-r5/identical-source-cost-control.json), also with five fresh
+browser observations per build and all competing audits closed, recorded a worst-time increase from
+1,924 to 2,143 ms despite equal source hashes. These measurements have variation. This control does
+not make a failed optimization pass, justify rerunning until favorable, or establish the cause of
+that variation. The strict observed median-and-worst gate remains unchanged.
+
+Candidate comparisons preserve the original source coordinates, RGB values, and probe membership.
+When geometry changes, those probes follow its current foreground depth. Lost fit confidence or
+thin-depth support is a regression; newly introduced cuts also enter the hole check. An 18-frame
+equivalence check reproduced the original native pixels and score components before these methods
+were used for research. The original finder, camera poses, calibration files, and thresholds are
+unchanged. The original-finder baseline is complete: 118 inputs, 236 profiles, and 2,124 color
+poses. An independent integrity check decoded and rehashed every native color frame, verified 10,620
+native artifact hashes, and checked every source photo hash. All native color pixels and quality
+values match the earlier atlas, whose different application source prevents treating that agreement
+as identical-source repeat noise. One operator-interrupted browser attempt is retained in the raw
+history alongside its successful retry.
+
+The repeat study was deliberately bounded to 72 actual paired input/profile repetitions across 36
+inputs. Its completed aggregation found zero differences in all 21 quality metrics. The other 164
+profiles receive zero acceptance tolerance in that initial record. An independent check decoded all
+648 repeated native color poses and rehashed all 3,240 artifacts; every repeated color pixel and
+quality value matches the baseline. Each original bounded capture flag remains unchanged. Additional
+captures and their actual final coverage are recorded separately in the
+[repeat evidence package](https://github.com/ryanjosephkamp/splashery/tree/codex/photo-3d-r5-clips/review/photo-3d-r5/verification).
+Unmeasured cases always retain zero tolerance; incomplete coverage is never called complete. The
+synchronized-main current-source study is complete: all 236 profiles, all 2,124 decoded native color
+frames, all 10,620 native-artifact hashes, and all 118 actual photo hashes passed independent
+verification. Every native color pixel and every quality value matches the baseline, with Sharp
+enabled and no recorded browser errors. The unchanged comparison reports zero regressions and
+exactly 0% reduction in each selected class. All three 25% targets therefore fail.
+
+The checkpoint's 49 clips contain 36 built-in inputs from the frozen corpus and 13 older review
+inputs outside it. A separate original-finder study verifies Sharp for those additional 13 inputs at
+both profiles, including 234 decoded native color poses and the original photo/depth hashes. All 131
+distinct inputs have working Sharp views at both profiles. These extra 26 profiles do not change
+frozen target membership, and they are not a before/after quality or cost measurement.
+
+All 49 checkpoint paired clips and five extra recordings are complete: 54 distinct videos, 72 actual
+native frame pairs each, and zero changed pixels across all 3,888 pairs. All 54 encoded files passed
+independent size, duration, frame-rate, frame-count, and SHA-256 checks; every video has at least 37
+distinct native frames. The
+[clips, credits, raw baseline, repeats, and integrity evidence](https://github.com/ryanjosephkamp/splashery/tree/codex/photo-3d-r5-clips/review/photo-3d-r5)
+are published on the media branch, never merged. The 15 selected inputs have complete recordings,
+and the complete 118-input ranking measures zero reduction on every input. Original manifest order
+breaks the measured ties for the first ten and last five slots; no ten actual improvements are
+claimed. The exact 49 input/view pairs and all 98 original photo/depth hashes also match the
+protected checkpoints. The original clips used four seconds, with 6 fps on 48 inputs and 12 fps on
+the forest. The fresh clips use six seconds and 12 fps throughout; identical timestamps or cadence
+are not claimed.
+
+Several approaches have already failed their gates:
+
+| Approach                                                   | Observed limit                                                                                                                                                                                    |
+| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| Reflected far-side texture continuation                    | Reduces some ribbons but can increase boundary color error or texture loss. A guarded variant still regressed on the forest and library.                                                          |
+| Finer source-depth silhouette clipping                     | The forest phone case improved some boundary and ribbon scores but increased fringe width. Narrower antialiasing still lost thin-line width or edge registration.                                 |
+| Projected or rendered foreground guards for fill           | Either regressed boundary error or left the worst quality scores unchanged; an extra render target also adds work and memory.                                                                     |
+| Preserving source-supported small, narrow depth components | A complete 236-profile depth-field screen found no improvement in the selected flat-depth or order warning means.                                                                                 |
+| Alternative DA3 depth estimates                            | On the frozen 209 flagged profiles, the Node depth-field screen worsened the flat-depth mean from 0.560372 to 0.618065, with 128 flat-depth and 59 order regressions. No replacement model ships. |
+| Several combined buffer and surface optimizations          | Exploratory phone timings were mixed. They do not establish a median-and-worst cost pass.                                                                                                         |
+
+The [complete builder equivalence record](photo-3d-r5/index-builder-equivalence.json) covers all 236
+input/profile combinations. A later
+[complete depth-stage diagnostic](photo-3d-r5/depth-stage-diagnostic.json) found that the upsampled
+field's flagged mean was 0.544247 versus the displayed field's 0.560372: only a 2.88% hypothetical
+flat-warning reduction, with 20 flat-warning and 143 order-warning regressions among those 209
+flagged profiles. Removing the later cleanup is therefore neither a 25% solution nor a safe repair.
+This diagnostic uses the original field and cue scorer; it is not a rendered quality or phone-cost
+measurement.
+
+All three subsequent combinations of guarded texture continuation with finer silhouette clipping
+also failed the forest phone regression screen, on fringe width, thin-line width, or registration.
+The [bounded render-research record](photo-3d-r5/rejected-render-research.json) identifies these and
+subsequent source-guarded silhouette and color-fallback rejections. Early rejection is not reported
+as full-corpus coverage.
+
+Four narrower foreground-mask footprints were also tested in native phone renders. The two-pixel
+variant reduced ribbons by 7.26% on the forest and 43.73% on the street without another measured
+quality regression on those two inputs, but increased the library's boundary error from 0.18480 to
+0.18741. A three-pixel footprint also increased library boundary error, and a one-pixel footprint
+increased forest palette excess. A four-pixel footprint preserved scores on all three bounded inputs
+but improved none of their selected worst-pose scores. All four were cut; these WebGL-only
+prototypes never became production or cost candidates. Their per-input gains and failures remain in
+the bounded render-research record.
+
+Two additional depth-guide variants failed on the forest phone profile. Removing the unsharp bias
+changed flattened junctions from 187 to 186, but reversed hypotheses from 46 to 47 out of 303. Point
+sampling changed them to 184 and 50. Neither survives the order gate. Two bounded local RGB/depth
+regression variants, constrained to supported model depths, were also cut within 11 profiles: one
+increased the spiral stairs' flat warning, and the stricter fit increased the wildflowers' order
+warning. These are depth-field screens, not rendered quality or cost passes.
+
+The new cold-cost tool uses two symmetric direct-file servers and the original finder's actual
+new-input Sharp completion fence, cover check, and PSS sampling window. It records fresh-browser
+observations separately, preserves failures, pins source and method hashes, and refuses to call a
+partial corpus or a non-isolated run a cost pass. An isolation-negative check correctly rejected a
+run while other captures were active. Protocol smoke measurements are not acceptance evidence. A
+separate four-observation protocol smoke completed with all other capture and browser processes
+closed. It verified isolation and browser teardown, but it is too small to establish the requested
+median-and-worst cost gate. No optimization has been accepted on its timings.
+
+Two execution-connection interruptions ended managed capture processes. Validated saved profiles
+were preserved and checked before reuse. Resume verifies source, settings, method snapshots, source
+probes, and every retained native artifact. An actual corrupted-copy check was rejected before a
+browser launched. A full-request early-stop bug in the new study controller was fixed: complete
+coverage now requires all inputs, both profiles, every pose, clean Sharp results, and all successful
+attempts. Saved review videos likewise require matching hashes and complete native-frame evidence;
+their manifests are written atomically.
+
+Two further native forest-phone screens also failed. Rebalancing the Sharp grid with the same cell
+capacity reduced boundary color error and texture loss, but increased ribbons, edge displacement,
+and transition width. Replacing the fill's Manhattan donor wavefront with an exact Euclidean search
+reduced ribbons from 0.57436 to 0.54752 and texture loss from 0.54242 to 0.42072, but increased
+boundary color error from 0.10307 to 0.10962, local palette excess, and thin-line width. Its
+distance transform matched brute force on 960 small fixtures, but numerical correctness does not
+make that rendered regression acceptable. Both variants were cut. Their records are in the same
+bounded render-research report.
+
+A complete [MoGe-2 depth-field study](photo-3d-r5/moge-depth-screen.json) covered all 76 built-in
+samples and 12 reference scenes at both profiles. Replacing the built-in depths caused 73 flat-depth
+and 95 order-warning regressions among 152 sample profiles. Even an optimistic choice of the better
+original or replacement result for each target profile could reduce the frozen flat-warning mean by
+only 2.66% before rendering and order gates, or 0.37% while preserving the order score. This is a
+feasibility bound, not a deployed per-input selection rule. Reported mean reference AbsRel fell by
+51.9%, but four reference RMSEs increased, and 23 pixels became unscored. The lower mean does not
+establish an overall quality improvement. No replacement model or baked asset ships. A separate
+[color-line depth continuation study](photo-3d-r5/color-line-depth-screen.json) changed 135
+displayed depth fields across 152 built-in profiles, but left every flat-depth and order-warning
+count unchanged. It was cut before native rendering and cost measurements.
+
+The [higher-detail MoGe follow-up](photo-3d-r5/moge-higher-detail-screen.json) used the same pinned
+weights at 3,600 tokens and a maximum input side of 1,024 pixels. Its bounded set contains three
+built-in samples and two reference scenes, both profiles. All six built-in sample/profile rows
+increased order warnings, and two increased flat warnings. Both reference RMSEs increased, and the
+fur reference lost 23 scored pixels. A large wildflowers flat-warning improvement therefore does not
+qualify the variant. It was cut; these ten rows are not full-corpus evidence.
+
+A [larger Depth Anything 3 Base screen](photo-3d-r5/da3-base-depth-screen.json) covered four
+built-in samples and two reference scenes at both profiles. Its pinned Apache 2.0 weights loaded
+strictly on the CPU. All eight built-in rows improved ordering warnings but increased flat warnings;

+fixed [detail-boost fusion](photo-3d-r5/multiscale-detail-boost-screen.json) reduced flat warnings
+on all eight built-in rows but increased order warnings on all eight. A separate
+[nine-variant filter-bank screen](photo-3d-r5/multiscale-filter-family-screen.json) replaced coarse
+high frequencies with model detail at three fixed scales, either fully or with model-agreement
+weights. None preserved both warning scores across the eight built-in rows. Its largest bounded

+ten fusion variants were cut before rendering and cost; no input-specific model switch is deployed.
+
+A [reference-endpoint diagnostic](photo-3d-r5/cue-truth-normalized-diagnostic.json) preserved every
+original cue count, then examined eligible optical-axis truth at those same endpoints. Among 2,820
+supported pairs, 1,398 original fields were flagged flat; 912 of those also have less than the
+unchanged 2% disparity separation after normalizing and quantizing the true inverse depths. Another
+1,554 pairs lack eligible reference support and remain excluded. This does not prove that any
+contour is false, assess reconstructed motion, or justify changing a threshold. The 12 reference
+scenes are excluded from the selected flat-warning target, so these counts cannot be transferred to
+its 209 profiles. They support investigating cue calibration separately from physical depth accuracy
+in a future task.
+
+The glass jug was the sole built-in MoGe result to improve both warning scores at both profiles. Its
+[native nine-pose phone check](photo-3d-r5/moge-glass-jug-native-rejection.json) nevertheless

+was cut immediately; a promising depth-field screen does not qualify a reconstruction.
+
+A bounded [Depth Anything V2 Large study](photo-3d-r5/da2-large-depth-screen.json) covered four
+built-in samples and two reference scenes at both profiles. It caused two built-in flat-warning
+regressions and six order regressions, while the still-life reference's AbsRel and RMSE also

+# Photo to 3D round 5: measured repair run
+
+Codex (GPT-6) carried out the repair research and verification for
+[task 93](../codex/93-photo-3d-r5.md) on `codex/photo-3d-r5`. The frozen main is
+`5a55f5ccc25ebfa155e5db2391236558feb551ec`, and the protected checkpoint is
+`58f3d8ede13714bf4b3d1f99fbf3b29d7f60e492`.
+
+The Goal began on October 15, 2026, at 9:33 p.m. Eastern (October 16 at 01:33 UTC). The hard stop is
+October 16 at 9:33 a.m. Eastern (13:33 UTC). **The Goal is unmet; no production change qualified.**
+
+## Status of the retained change
+
+| Requirement                                                          | Measured result                                                                                                                                                               |
+| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| Three chosen classes improve by at least 25%                         | Unmet: boundary color error, flat-depth warnings, and ribbons each improve by exactly 0%.                                                                                     |
+| Every other atlas input and checkpoint clip stays the same or better | Preserved: all 118 inputs at both profiles have identical native pixels and quality values; all 49 checkpoint pairs match across the review frames.                           |
+| Phone time and memory do not increase                                | No runtime change is retained. Every tested optimization was cut; the complete phone-cost gate and physical-phone performance are unmeasured.                                 |
+| Sharp works for every input at both profiles                         | Verified for all 118 atlas inputs and 13 additional legacy review inputs, or 131 distinct inputs.                                                                             |
+| Every existing spec passes                                           | All 2,853 runnable tests passed after one failed-job rerun on the cited revision. One existing private-fixture test remains skipped, so every-spec coverage is unestablished. |
+| Ten most-improved and five least-improved review slots               | All 15 slots have recordings. The complete 118-input ranking contains measured zero-improvement ties; no ten actual improvements are claimed.                                 |
+
+The application, sample assets, vendor files, original finder, and existing tests remain unchanged
+from synchronized main. Eight new spec files contain the 26 measurement-method tests. Rejected
+prototype code is archived as text on the unmerged review branch and is not included in the app.
+Final additional repeat coverage is recorded in the linked evidence package and the PR handback;
+partial captures never grant tolerance to an unmeasured case.
+
+## Target selection and correction
+
+The [118-input atlas](photo-3d-failures-2026-10.md) supplies the frozen source hashes, nine poses,
+two profiles, probes, metric definitions, and review levels. A row is one input at one profile. For
+each class, cost is the flagged row count times its mean severity, where severity is the row's worst
+supported pose score divided by that class's existing review level. Equivalently, cost is the sum of
+these ratios over flagged rows. This is a repair-priority heuristic, not a perceptually calibrated
+comparison between unlike units. The initial ranking omitted the atlas's separate flat-depth warning
+filter. Including that filter corrects the three highest costs as follows. This correction does not
+move the original deadline; no production reconstruction change was retained under the initial
+selection.
+
+| Class                                | Flagged / supported rows |        Mean flagged score |     Cost | Intended repair                                                                                                                        |
+| ------------------------------------ | -----------------------: | ------------------------: | -------: | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| Color error at depth boundaries      |                227 / 227 |        13.4661% RGB error | 764.2023 | Inspect source-color ownership and depth-edge registration; preserve text, thin structures, and probe support.                         |
+| Flat-depth T-junction warnings       |                209 / 212 | 56.0372% warned junctions | 585.5884 | Investigate source-supported depth separation with frozen baseline probes; texture junctions alone cannot justify new geometric steps. |
+| Directional ribbons in revealed fill |                211 / 223 | 40.3048 percentage points | 566.9536 | Continue eligible background texture into disocclusions while preserving gradients and believable content.                             |
+
+The remaining costs are texture-energy loss 232.1019, fringe width 195.4848, lost thin-line contrast
+173.5949, memory 138.8500, depth-order warnings 124.1080, cold latency 53.3361, and zero flagged
+holes or default-threshold reference-depth errors. The exploratory 5% reference-depth cutoff has a
+cost of 20.1228 and does not affect the selected targets. Flat-depth and order warnings are
+image-cue hypotheses, not measurements of physical scene depth. Reference errors remain separate.
+Unsupported scores remain unknown. Both profiles and every input remain regression gates.
+
+The atlas examples include the dog's muzzle and ears, the dragonfly, and the long library for
+boundary error; submerged stones, the frozen waterfall, and the fishing cove for flat-depth
+warnings; and the forest path, the still-life painting, and the tabby for ribbons. The exact flagged
+membership and scores are recorded in [the target manifest](photo-3d-r5/targets.json).
+
+## Verification plan
+
+Re-measure frozen main with the original finder, measure repeat noise, and compare candidates using
+the same input hashes and native rendered evidence. Reject any supported per-input regression, lost
+probe support, blank capture, changed test threshold, or phone cost increase. Keep metric
+calibration separate from visual review. Phone-profile software rendering is not a measurement on a
+physical phone. The final handback will distinguish completed checks from missing evidence.
+
+## Measured research
+
+The production reconstruction source is still unchanged. None of the three 25% targets has passed.
+Source-only experiments stay outside the shipping tree until their quality, cost, and motion gates
+pass.
+
+Main advanced to `cc297c89ef4fa4bf04e43196ca3b37e39c97a372` during the run. It was merged into this
+branch without conflicts. That merge changes application lifecycle and unrelated toys, but not the
+Photo to 3D core, relief, depth model, or finder calibration. The original frozen-main study
+completed without changing its measurement source. A fresh full current-source study uses the
+synchronized application rather than mixing captures from different application revisions. All
+production reconstruction source, sample assets, and vendor files remain identical to synchronized
+main; no runtime optimization is retained.
+
+The compressed-index candidate matched every pure-builder output across all 236 input/profile
+combinations, but its isolated forest cost study failed. Five fresh browser observations per build
+produced median/worst first-view times of 4,186/4,631 ms on main and 4,691/9,828 ms on the
+candidate. PSS improved, but the observed time increase fails the gate. It was cut; the
+[observations and hashes](photo-3d-r5/index-cost-rejection.json) remain available. These are
+one-input counterexamples, not a complete-corpus cost measurement or proof of a causal slowdown.
+
+A second exact-output candidate deferred the plain bilinear fallback until the weighted depth gather
+actually needs it. Its [complete comparison](photo-3d-r5/lazy-bilinear-equivalence.json) matched
+every returned property across all 236 builds, plus 32 explicit fallback fixtures. Its
+[isolated cost study](photo-3d-r5/lazy-bilinear-cost-rejection.json) improved median/worst time from
+3,681/4,257 to 2,984/3,938 ms, but increased median/worst PSS from 801/814 to 818/841 MiB, so it was
+cut. Combining it with
+[parent termination of uncached workers](photo-3d-r5/parent-termination-cost-rejection.json) reduced
+memory but increased both time statistics. A separate
+[self-closing worker variant](photo-3d-r5/self-closing-cost-rejection.json) also reduced memory, but
+its observed worst time increased from 3,537 to 3,620 ms. Both were cut. Browser protocol probes
+verified identical returned payloads and surviving transferred bitmap pixels, cached-worker reuse,
+and stale-token fallback; those probes do not replace full-corpus cost and motion checks.
+
+Two later exact-output candidates also failed isolated cost screens. The existing
+[canvas fallback](photo-3d-r5/canvas-fallback-cost-rejection.json) matched all 18 forest native
+poses at both profiles, but median/worst first-view time rose from 2,016/2,267 to 2,344/2,548 ms,
+and worst PSS rose from 841 to 864 MiB. The
+[scratch-gradient cache](photo-3d-r5/scratch-gradient-equivalence.json) matched every prepared and
+unprepared builder output and source-preparation object across all 236 input/profile combinations.
+Its [1,296 direct refiner fixtures](photo-3d-r5/scratch-gradient-fixtures.json) exercised cache
+hits, precision fallback, and boundary fallback, independently matching the pinned original helper
+byte for byte. The separate 32 fixtures in the builder record exercise the unchanged upsampler
+fallback. Its 18-pose native scout was also pixel-exact. Nevertheless, its
+[forest cost screen](photo-3d-r5/scratch-gradient-cost-rejection.json) increased median/worst time
+from 1,628/1,640 to 1,734/1,860 ms and median/worst PSS from 813/852 to 838/852 MiB; the exact worst
+PSS increase was 267,264 bytes. Each screen used five fresh browsers per build with competing local
+audits closed. Both candidates were cut without benchmark retries. These are bounded observed
+rejections, not a full-corpus performance result or a causal slowdown claim.
+[Exact candidate and method bytes, raw cost manifests, and every observation](https://github.com/ryanjosephkamp/splashery/tree/codex/photo-3d-r5-clips/review/photo-3d-r5/rejected-code-research)
+are preserved on the unmerged review branch.
+
+An [identical-source control](photo-3d-r5/identical-source-cost-control.json), also with five fresh
+browser observations per build and all competing audits closed, recorded a worst-time increase from
+1,924 to 2,143 ms despite equal source hashes. These measurements have variation. This control does
+not make a failed optimization pass, justify rerunning until favorable, or establish the cause of
+that variation. The strict observed median-and-worst gate remains unchanged.
+
+Candidate comparisons preserve the original source coordinates, RGB values, and probe membership.
+When geometry changes, those probes follow its current foreground depth. Lost fit confidence or
+thin-depth support is a regression; newly introduced cuts also enter the hole check. An 18-frame
+equivalence check reproduced the original native pixels and score components before these methods
+were used for research. The original finder, camera poses, calibration files, and thresholds are
+unchanged. The original-finder baseline is complete: 118 inputs, 236 profiles, and 2,124 color
+poses. An independent integrity check decoded and rehashed every native color frame, verified 10,620
+native artifact hashes, and checked every source photo hash. All native color pixels and quality
+values match the earlier atlas, whose different application source prevents treating that agreement
+as identical-source repeat noise. One operator-interrupted browser attempt is retained in the raw
+history alongside its successful retry.
+
+The repeat study was deliberately bounded to 72 actual paired input/profile repetitions across 36
+inputs. Its completed aggregation found zero differences in all 21 quality metrics. The other 164
+profiles receive zero acceptance tolerance in that initial record. An independent check decoded all
+648 repeated native color poses and rehashed all 3,240 artifacts; every repeated color pixel and
+quality value matches the baseline. Each original bounded capture flag remains unchanged. Additional
+captures and their actual final coverage are recorded separately in the
+[repeat evidence package](https://github.com/ryanjosephkamp/splashery/tree/codex/photo-3d-r5-clips/review/photo-3d-r5/verification).
+Unmeasured cases always retain zero tolerance; incomplete coverage is never called complete. The
+synchronized-main current-source study is complete: all 236 profiles, all 2,124 decoded native color
+frames, all 10,620 native-artifact hashes, and all 118 actual photo hashes passed independent
+verification. Every native color pixel and every quality value matches the baseline, with Sharp
+enabled and no recorded browser errors. The unchanged comparison reports zero regressions and
+exactly 0% reduction in each selected class. All three 25% targets therefore fail.
+
+The checkpoint's 49 clips contain 36 built-in inputs from the frozen corpus and 13 older review
+inputs outside it. A separate original-finder study verifies Sharp for those additional 13 inputs at
+both profiles, including 234 decoded native color poses and the original photo/depth hashes. All 131
+distinct inputs have working Sharp views at both profiles. These extra 26 profiles do not change
+frozen target membership, and they are not a before/after quality or cost measurement.
+
+All 49 checkpoint paired clips and five extra recordings are complete: 54 distinct videos, 72 actual
+native frame pairs each, and zero changed pixels across all 3,888 pairs. All 54 encoded files passed
+independent size, duration, frame-rate, frame-count, and SHA-256 checks; every video has at least 37
+distinct native frames. The
+[clips, credits, raw baseline, repeats, and integrity evidence](https://github.com/ryanjosephkamp/splashery/tree/codex/photo-3d-r5-clips/review/photo-3d-r5)
+are published on the media branch, never merged. The 15 selected inputs have complete recordings,
+and the complete 118-input ranking measures zero reduction on every input. Original manifest order
+breaks the measured ties for the first ten and last five slots; no ten actual improvements are
+claimed. The exact 49 input/view pairs and all 98 original photo/depth hashes also match the
+protected checkpoints. The original clips used four seconds, with 6 fps on 48 inputs and 12 fps on
+the forest. The fresh clips use six seconds and 12 fps throughout; identical timestamps or cadence
+are not claimed.
+
